dossier.public_summary: A shallow 1.5-day flat-bottomed dip recurs 85 times on the target star with a planet size of about 1.4 Earth radii, no odd/even difference and no secondary eclipse. Centroid imaging confirms the dip is on the target and rules out nearby stars that could mimic it. The best explanation is a small planet.

reasons.why: Difference imaging puts the dip on the target; all neighbours that could fake it are ruled out (>3.5 sigma away, closest suspect 3.5 sigma from centroid).

Strongly flat-bottomed (negative v_sigma) favours a planetary transit over a V-shaped grazing EB; fit_b=0.03436, fit_k=0.0174, fit_chi2_red=1.016, duration.ratio=0.7822 matches central_h=1.589 for a 0.6719 Rsun star without needing density adjustment.

Undiluted depth 355.4 ppm gives rp_rstar=0.01885 => 1.382 Re, well below the stellar regime and below the 10 Re planet/giant boundary; sector depths steady p_constant=0.9527 with 85 transits snr=13.66, share=0.06532.
Odd depth 280 ppm vs even 305.7 ppm differ only 25.77 ppm at 0.55 sigma, with sector_oe_max_sigma=1.512 and sector_oe_sectors_over_3=0, arguing against an EB at twice the 1.51 d period.

No significant secondary (snr 3.638 well below 5, best_brightening_snr=1.909, depth_over_dip=0.2626) and sector_sec_half_max_snr=1.114 with positive_share=0.5; combined with flat shape argues against a stellar companion on target.
